question: Which body part is mainly affected in Type I FGM?

options.A: The outer labia majora only
options.B: The Bartholin glands
options.C: The clitoris and its prepuce
options.D: The entire vaginal wall

question: A researcher studying a rare illness asks current patients to bring in friends or family members with the same condition. What is this called?

options.A: Quota sampling
options.B: Simple random sampling
options.C: Snowball sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: You got it! Just like a snowball rolling downhill gets bigger, participants help you recruit more participants from their network. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T17#GNS224_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the very first step in the disease surveillance cycle?

options.A: Data generation and collection
options.B: Writing a newspaper advertisement
options.C: Publishing a textbook on epidemiology
options.D: Allocating national budget funds

explanation: It all starts right at the frontline! Nurses and health workers spot and record cases, kicking off the whole surveillance process. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h4)

question: What does the thermic effect of food (TEF) refer to?

options.A: The heat lost through the skin during a fever
options.B: The calories burned during cardiovascular exercise
options.C: The basal energy used by the liver during sleep
options.D: The energy used to process and digest nutrients

explanation: Your body actually burns calories just chewing, digesting, and processing food. That's what we call TEF! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h4)

question: If a student wants to study how hospital room ventilation and fresh air affect patient healing, which theory fits best?

options.A: Callista Roy’s Adaptation Model
options.B: Dorothea Orem’s Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Florence Nightingale’s Environmental Theory
options.D: Madeleine Leininger’s Culture Care Theory

explanation: You nailed it! Nightingale was the pioneer of using clean air, light, and a healthy environment to help patients recover. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h4)

question: A patient with locked-in syndrome can't speak or move, but blinks to answer questions. What is the most important first nursing action?

options.A: Assume the patient cannot understand instructions given in the room.
options.B: Establish a reliable communication system using eye movements.
options.C: Limit neurological checks to once every twenty-four hours.
options.D: Administer heavy sedation to reduce patient awareness.

explanation: Even though they can't speak, these patients are fully conscious! Setting up a simple blink-for-yes system brings them immense comfort and dignity. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h6)

question: What does the 'structure' component of the Donabedian model refer to?

options.A: The steps taken to administer an injection
options.B: The final recovery rate of the patient
options.C: The hospital environment, staff, and equipment
options.D: The financial profit of the clinic

explanation: Easy peasy! In the Donabedian model, 'structure' is the foundation—it's about the tools, buildings, and skilled staff we have available to do our work. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h3)

question: To call leprosy 'paucibacillary', what is the highest number of skin lesions a patient can have?

options.A: Ten lesions
options.B: Twenty lesions
options.C: Five lesions
options.D: Two lesions

explanation: Great job! 'Pauci' means few. Having 5 or fewer skin lesions puts it in the paucibacillary category. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the expected effect of acute blood loss on a patient's pulse rate?

options.A: The pulse rate stays completely normal until death occurs
options.B: The pulse rate drops sharply to conserve remaining blood
options.C: The pulse rate increases to maintain blood pressure
options.D: The pulse rhythm becomes permanently irregular and slow

explanation: When blood volume drops, the body compensates by increasing the heart rate to keep vital organs supplied with blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is a major community-wide effect when a clinic suffers an outbreak of healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Loss of public trust in the healthcare system
options.B: Lower costs for public health insurance programs
options.C: An immediate surplus of available hospital beds
options.D: Increased willingness of patients to receive injections

explanation: Exactly. When a clinic spreads disease instead of healing, people lose faith and may stop seeking care when they truly need it. Safe nursing builds community trust! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h5)

question: An IV infusion of 1000 mL normal saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using an electronic pump. What is the rate in mL/hr?

options.A: 125 mL/hr
options.B: 150 mL/hr
options.C: 100 mL/hr
options.D: 80 mL/hr

explanation: Divide the total volume (1000 mL) by the total hours (8 hours) to get 125 mL/hr. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why is balancing the cash register at the end of a shift so important in a DRF unit?

options.A: To prove that the nurses worked longer hours than scheduled
options.B: To ensure that cash collected matches the volume of drugs dispensed
options.C: To decide which drugs are most popular among patients
options.D: To calculate the monthly salary bonus for the nursing staff

explanation: Daily cash reconciliation keeps things transparent, honest, and ensures every single tablet is accounted for. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which nutrient is especially important early in pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Sodium chloride
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Potassium

explanation: Correct! Folic acid is a hero in early pregnancy because it helps the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h6)

question: Why are community health nurses in a great position to spot children at risk of delinquency?

options.A: They possess the exclusive legal authority to arrest young lawbreakers
options.B: They interact with families across homes, schools, and clinics regularly
options.C: They spend most of their working hours inside maximum-security prisons
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers trained in psychological diagnosis

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses visit homes, schools, and clinics, they see family dynamics firsthand and can catch early warning signs. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why should you gently swirl a mixed vaccine vial instead of shaking it hard?

options.A: Gentle swirling makes the liquid change colors faster
options.B: Vigorous shaking creates foam and can break down fragile vaccine proteins
options.C: Shaking causes the glass vial to shatter inside the syringe
options.D: Shaking releases dangerous toxic gases into the clinic air

explanation: Think of vaccine proteins like delicate structures—shaking them too hard tears them apart and ruins the medication! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h4)

question: Why is community outreach such an important part of psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It allows nurses to avoid working inside hospitals entirely
options.B: It brings mental health resources directly to vulnerable populations who may not seek care
options.C: It replaces the need for individual counseling sessions
options.D: It guarantees that no one in the community will ever feel sad

explanation: Not everyone can walk into a hospital for help. Outreach bridges the gap and brings care straight to the people who need it most. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which of these is a classic example of appropriate technology in a Nigerian primary health care setting?

options.A: Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) using clean water, salt, and sugar
options.B: A computerized robotic surgical theater in a remote village clinic
options.C: Imported synthetic infant formula distributed without clean water access
options.D: An underground nuclear-powered diagnostic laboratory

explanation: Correct! ORT is a lifesaver because it is scientifically proven, cheap, safe, and mothers can easily mix it at home using everyday ingredients. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which condition is classified as a hyperkinetic movement disorder?

options.A: Huntington's disease
options.B: Spinal shock
options.C: Parkinson's disease
options.D: Flaccid paralysis

explanation: Huntington's disease features excess, involuntary movements like chorea, placing it in the hyperkinetic category of movement disorders. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why is proper stock forecasting and inventory management so critical in family planning clinics?

options.A: It stops clients from asking questions about side effects
options.B: It removes the need for keeping any written client logs
options.C: It guarantees that contraceptives will expire on clinic shelves
options.D: It prevents stockouts and ensures continuous client protection

explanation: Keeping track of inventory means supplies never run out when a client walks in, preventing accidental gaps in protection. Smart logistics! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h7)

question: How should a nurse leader respond when frontline staff push back against a new QI project?

options.A: Force immediate compliance without offering any explanation
options.B: Report them immediately to hospital human resources for insubordination
options.C: Listen to their concerns with empathy to find practical flaws
options.D: Ignore the complaints because resistance always fades away

explanation: That's right! Staff pushback often points out real problems in the daily workflow that leadership missed. It's helpful feedback, not just stubbornness. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h6)

question: A clinical instructor tells students to use a case they saw last week to understand a new patient's symptoms. Which theory is this?

options.A: Classical conditioning
options.B: Constructivism
options.C: Rote memorization
options.D: Behaviorism

explanation: Constructivism means 'building' new knowledge on top of what you already know and experienced before. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U8_T2#GST321_U8_T2_h3)

question: Why is early recognition of genitourinary growths so important?

options.A: It directly improves survival rates and quality of life
options.B: It guarantees that the tumor will remain completely benign
options.C: It completely prevents the need for any future blood tests
options.D: It ensures the patient will never require surgical intervention

explanation: Catching these growths early gives our patients the best fighting chance. Prompt care stops things from getting worse and helps keep them comfortable and healthy. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why is community engagement important for adolescent health programs?

options.A: It forces all teenagers in the neighborhood to visit the hospital daily
options.B: It gives the nursing staff extra financial bonuses from the local government
options.C: It eliminates the need for any trained medical personnel in the clinic
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures long-term support for sensitive health topics

explanation: Involving community leaders and parents prevents resistance and builds strong local backing for youth programs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h8)

question: What special type of tissue lines the inside of the ureter so it can stretch?

options.A: Simple squamous epithelium
options.B: Transitional epithelium

options.D: Simple columnar epithelium

explanation: You're learning fast! Transitional epithelium is amazing because it stretches easily as fluid passes through. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T2#GNS121_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does cervical mucus look and feel like right around the time of ovulation?

options.A: Thin and watery with a strong foul odor
options.B: Dry, crumbly, and dark brown in color
options.C: Clear, stretchy, and slippery like raw egg whites
options.D: Thick, sticky, and opaque like paste

explanation: High estrogen makes fertile mucus stretchy and slippery—just like raw egg white—to help sperm swim up easily. Nature is amazing! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h3)

question: What are the bumpy, distinct sections seen on the mother's side of a delivered placenta called?

options.A: Cotyledons
options.B: Decidual cells
options.C: Spiral arteries
options.D: Chorionic villi

explanation: You'll see this often in the maternity ward! The maternal side of the placenta is divided into about 15 to 20 carved sections known as cotyledons. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T4#GNS121_U6_T4_h5)

question: A patient with urge incontinence is starting a bladder retraining program. What is the right instruction to give them?

options.A: Stop doing pelvic floor exercises completely
options.B: Hold urine for as long as possible until severe pain occurs
options.C: Drink large amounts of water only right before bedtime
options.D: Urinate on a strict schedule, slowly increasing the time between trips

explanation: Bladder retraining uses a set schedule that slowly stretches out the time between bathroom breaks, helping the bladder hold more without sudden spasms. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h6)

question: If a virus has a strict 14-day incubation period, how long must close contacts be watched?

options.A: Fourteen full days from the last time they were exposed
options.B: Just three days, because most people fall sick fast
options.C: Until a lab test comes back negative
options.D: Only until the first afternoon they feel tired

explanation: Monitoring has to cover the entire possible window to catch late bloomers before they can spread the virus in the community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h5)

question: A woman's last menstrual period began on January 1st. Using Naegele's rule, what is her estimated date of delivery (EDD)?

options.A: September 15th
options.B: November 5th
options.C: October 8th
options.D: December 25th

explanation: Easy trick: add 7 days to the first day of the last period, then subtract 3 months. Jan 1st + 7 days = Jan 8th, minus 3 months = October 8th! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h4)

question: A patient suddenly has wild, flailing movements in one arm and leg after a stroke. Which brain area is likely affected?

options.A: The anterior thalamus
options.B: The subthalamic nucleus
options.C: The optic chiasm
options.D: The pineal gland

explanation: You got it! Damage to the subthalamic nucleus can lead to hemiballismus—a condition causing sudden, forceful, flailing limb movements. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T19#GNS211_U3_T19_h5)

question: Why is it best to use both quantitative and qualitative methods during your community assessment?

options.A: It is required by law to spend extra ministry funding
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to speak to villagers directly
options.C: It combines measurable statistics with deep human context
options.D: It ensures that no written reports need to be created

explanation: Numbers give you the stats (how many people are sick), but talking to people gives you the story (why they are sick and what stops them from getting help). You need both! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why do doctors still order lab tests even when a male patient's physical symptoms look obvious?

options.A: Hospitals require blood tests for insurance billing purposes
options.B: Different STIs can present with very similar clinical signs
options.C: Antibiotics will not work without a written laboratory report
options.D: Physical exams cannot detect any form of genital infection

explanation: Many STIs look identical on the outside (like causing the same discharge or sores). Lab tests tell us the exact germ so we use the right drug. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the main role of a nurse when a patient is referred for genetic counseling?

options.A: Prescribing gene-therapy medications to correct mutations
options.B: Providing the final diagnosis for the genetic disorder
options.C: Preparing the patient emotionally and clarifying basic hereditary concepts
options.D: Deciding whether the couple should have children

explanation: Nurses help bridge the gap by supporting the patient's emotional state and ensuring they understand why they are seeing the specialist. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h3)

question: Why is family caregiver education such a vital part of home health nursing?

options.A: Caregivers are legally required to pass nursing board examinations
options.B: Caregivers handle daily care routines during the many hours professionals are absent
options.C: Physicians require family members to sign off on all medical orders
options.D: Education allows family members to replace paid aides entirely

explanation: Because healthcare staff are only present briefly, family caregivers must be taught how to manage routines safely when alone. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why are spinal reflexes so crucial for our survival?

options.A: They help the brain store long-term memories of physical skills
options.B: They allow quick reactions to danger without waiting for brain processing
options.C: They control conscious thoughts about body movement
options.D: They produce all the hormones needed for physical activity

explanation: Reflexes are life-savers! They bypass the slow process of thinking, letting your body react instantly to danger—like pulling your hand away from a hot iron before you even realize it burns. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h6)

question: What is a major barrier that prevents teenagers from visiting clinics for contraceptives?

options.A: The high academic performance required to enter clinics
options.B: Mandatory free transport provided to all school children
options.C: A complete absence of any illness during adolescence
options.D: Fear of judgmental staff and lack of confidentiality

explanation: Many teens avoid clinics because they fear being scolded by healthcare workers or having their visits reported to their parents. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h8)

question: A pregnant patient refuses to eat meat because she heard it causes birth defects. How should you handle this as her nurse?

options.A: Force her to eat the meat immediately during the clinic visit
options.B: Scold the patient for believing foolish stories
options.C: Recognize this as a cultural myth and gently offer safe protein alternatives
options.D: Ignore her diet since beliefs have no impact on pregnancy

explanation: Always respect your patient's background! Providing gentle, accurate education and helping them find alternative protein sources builds great trust. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h3)

question: What sign would you most expect in a patient with a low platelet count?

options.A: Stiff neck and high fever spikes
options.B: Bounding pulses and warm skin
options.C: Petechiae and bleeding gums
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the sclera

explanation: Platelets help us stop bleeding. When they're low, tiny red spots (petechiae) or bleeding gums show us that clotting isn't happening properly. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h2)

question: How does the uterus typically feel when assessing a patient with puerperal sepsis?

options.A: Soft, boggy, tender, and larger than expected for the postpartum day
options.B: Displaced entirely to the left side with no tenderness
options.C: Firm, contracted, non-tender, and well below the umbilicus
options.D: Completely rigid like a board with absent bowel sounds

explanation: Infection slows down normal uterine shrinking (involution). Instead of feeling firm, a septic uterus often feels soft, bulky, and painful when you touch it. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h4)

question: How does progesterone help protect an early pregnancy?

options.A: By stimulating the rapid shedding of the endometrial lining
options.B: By causing a sudden drop in core body temperature
options.C: By stopping all pituitary hormone release
options.D: By relaxing uterine smooth muscle to prevent early contractions

explanation: Progesterone acts like a calming agent for the uterus, keeping the muscles relaxed so a newly implanted embryo can stay safe and secure. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h3)

question: What does the famous saying 'the dose makes the poison' mean?

options.A: Small amounts of deadly poisons are always beneficial for health
options.B: Any substance can become harmful if the amount taken is too large
options.C: Only synthetic chemicals manufactured in laboratories are truly toxic
options.D: The chemical structure of a drug changes once inside the human stomach

explanation: Even safe things like water can become dangerous if you take too much of them at once. Toxicity is all about the quantity! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h1)

question: How does psychoeducation help a struggling family during a medical crisis?

options.A: It replaces the need for doctors to talk to the patient
options.B: It reduces anxiety caused by the unknown by explaining the condition
options.C: It completely pays off all accumulated hospital and pharmacy bills
options.D: It forces family members to hide their true feelings from staff

explanation: Providing clear, understandable information about a disease helps families feel more prepared and less frightened about what to expect. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the difference between substandard and counterfeit medications?

options.A: Substandard drugs are manufactured locally, while counterfeit drugs are always imported.
options.B: Counterfeit drugs are cheaper versions of safe generics produced by licensed companies.
options.C: Substandard drugs fail quality specifications, while counterfeit drugs are deliberately mislabeled copies.
options.D: Substandard drugs have expired dates, while counterfeit drugs contain too much active ingredient.

explanation: Substandard drugs are usually genuine products that missed quality marks, while counterfeits are fake, fraudulent copies made to deceive us. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary energy substrate used by the fetus, supplied constantly across the placenta?

options.A: Lactic acid
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Triglycerides
options.D: Amino acids

explanation: Glucose crosses the placenta easily and serves as the main fuel source for fetal metabolism and overall growth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h5)

question: Which type of illness spreads the fastest in crowded, poorly sanitized relief camps?

options.A: Degenerative joint diseases
options.B: Chronic autoimmune conditions
options.C: Waterborne infectious diseases
options.D: Hereditary metabolic disorders

explanation: Spot on! When clean water and toilets break down, infections like cholera and dysentery spread through the camp like wildfire. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why are hospital utility bills counted as 'indirect costs'?

options.A: They are shared across the facility and cannot be tied to one patient
options.B: They are paid directly by the nursing department
options.C: They only apply to private hospital rooms
options.D: They change every single day based on the weather

explanation: Things like electricity and water keep the whole hospital running for everyone, so you can't assign them to just one single patient's bill. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main artery that brings oxygen-rich blood to the tongue?

options.A: Facial artery
options.B: Maxillary artery
options.C: Lingual artery
options.D: Ascending pharyngeal artery

explanation: Easy to remember—'lingual' means tongue, so the lingual artery is the main blood supplier for tongue tissues! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h5)

question: A clinic has very little money and must choose between buying new office chairs or running a child immunization drive. What should come first?

options.A: Splitting the money evenly so neither project is fully completed
options.B: Returning the funds to the government to avoid making a choice
options.C: The office chairs because administrative comfort improves staff mood
options.D: The child immunization drive because it prevents disease outbreaks

explanation: You nailed it! Protecting kids from deadly diseases brings a huge public health win compared to upgrading office furniture. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why do nurses love using line diagrams instead of long tables of numbers to track trends?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need to collect raw numerical data.
options.B: They are the only graphic allowed in international nursing journals.
options.C: They prevent any mathematical errors from happening during data entry.
options.D: They make it much easier to spot upward or downward movement at a single glance.

explanation: Exactly! Pictures speak louder than numbers. A quick look at a line lets your brain grasp the whole story instantly. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T10#GNS217_U4_T10_h1)

question: Which nerve is most vulnerable to being stretched or compressed during a tough vaginal delivery?

options.A: Sciatic nerve
options.B: Pudendal nerve
options.C: Femoral nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: You're learning fast! The pudendal nerve runs right through the birth canal area, making it easy to stretch or compress during labor. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h3)

question: What is the main job of the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscle movements
options.B: Promoting digestion and nutrient absorption at rest
options.C: Regulating the body's internal temperature during sleep
options.D: Preparing the body for stressful or emergency situations

explanation: Think of the sympathetic system as your body's 'fight-or-flight' alarm. It gets you ready to act fast when danger or heavy stress shows up. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T30#GNS211_U3_T30_h1)

question: What key daily habit should you always stress to a patient taking an expectorant?

options.A: Avoiding all physical exercise
options.B: Eating a high-protein diet at night
options.C: Drinking plenty of water daily
options.D: Sleeping flat on the back

question: What dangerous action must nurses warn patients NEVER to do with a maggot-filled skin boil?

options.A: Applying cold compresses to reduce swelling before treatment
options.B: Squeezing or crushing the lesion aggressively with bare hands
options.C: Covering the area loosely with clean cotton gauze
options.D: Washing the surrounding skin gently with clean water and soap

question: What is the main job of the methodology section in a research proposal?

options.A: To list every book ever written on nursing
options.B: To praise previous researchers in the field
options.C: To prove that the researcher has a large budget
options.D: To explain how the study will be carried out

explanation: The methodology is your step-by-step game plan. It explains the exact tools, steps, and designs you will use to gather and check your data. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a common side effect of anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Constipation
options.B: Excessive saliva production
options.C: Urinary retention
options.D: Dry mouth

question: Why would a healthcare planner choose a Cost-Utility Analysis over a regular Cost-Effectiveness Analysis?

options.A: To calculate only the direct financial profits of a new pharmacy wing
options.B: To evaluate treatments that impact both length of life and patient well-being
options.C: To prove that all medical interventions cost the exact same amount
options.D: To avoid measuring clinical outcomes entirely in hospital settings

question: What is often the very first sign a woman might notice with early cervical cancer?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Complete cessation of urine output
options.C: Severe swelling in both feet
options.D: Sudden loss of scalp hair

explanation: Spot on! Bleeding between periods, after intercourse, or after menopause is a classic red flag that means 'time to see a doctor.' [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h4)

question: Which of these is a major physical trigger that can push a mum into distress during labour?

options.A: High pre-pregnancy weight
options.B: Early rupture of membranes
options.C: Prolonged labour
options.D: Low maternal height

explanation: When labour goes on for too long, a mum's physical and emotional energy tanks are bound to empty out, leading straight to distress. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h3)

question: In community health, why can't just one type of health worker solve every problem?

options.A: Government policies forbid single-worker clinics
options.B: Doctors lack the training to visit local neighborhoods
options.C: Nurses refuse to handle community cases on their own
options.D: Community issues involve physical, social, and economic factors

question: A patient shows signs of liver trouble after starting a new drug. Which of these should you NOT do?

explanation: Primary Health Care aims to bring essential health services as close as possible to where people live, making preventive measures like vaccines easily accessible. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: How does general palliative care differ from standard hospice care?

options.A: Palliative care is only provided in outpatient clinics, while hospice care is strictly for hospital inpatients.
options.B: Palliative care can be given alongside curative treatments, whereas hospice care begins when curative treatment has stopped.
options.C: Palliative care is managed entirely by physicians, whereas hospice care is run strictly by volunteers.
options.D: Palliative care focuses exclusively on spiritual counseling, while hospice care manages physical pain.

explanation: You nailed it! Think of hospice as a specific type of palliative care reserved for the final phase of life, while general palliative care can start on day one. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h8)

question: What protective gear is a must when handling strong, concentrated chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Sterile surgical gown and shoe covers
options.B: Heavy-duty utility gloves and eye protection
options.C: Clean non-sterile examination gloves
options.D: A standard paper surgical facemask only

explanation: Concentrated disinfectants can sting your skin and damage your eyes. Always wear heavy utility gloves and eye protection! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h8)

question: How do major community accidents immediately affect local hospitals and clinics?

options.A: By eliminating the need for surgical supplies
options.B: By overwhelming emergency wards and depleting blood banks
options.C: By reducing the overall cost of running the hospital
options.D: By increasing the number of available nurses on duty

explanation: A sudden rush of trauma patients can quickly stretch hospital supplies, staff, and blood reserves to their limits. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the real difference between just hearing someone talk and active listening?

options.A: Active listening can only be performed in a quiet hospital office.
options.B: Hearing requires the nurse to offer immediate medical diagnoses.
options.C: Active listening involves full concentration on both words and underlying emotions.
options.D: Hearing requires the nurse to write down every spoken word verbatim.

explanation: Active listening means tuning into the feelings behind the words, not just waiting for your turn to speak. Great nurses master this! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h4)

question: Which document tells a nurse NOT to start CPR on an unresponsive patient?

options.A: A general medical insurance policy
options.B: A valid do-not-resuscitate order
options.C: A verbal request from a distant relative
options.D: A standard hospital admission form

explanation: Always respect patient wishes! A signed and valid Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) order or advance directive legally stops us from initiating CPR. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h9)

question: According to the Swiss Cheese Model, what usually causes patient harm?

options.A: A combination of multiple small system failures
options.B: Unavoidable natural deterioration of medical tools
options.C: Sudden refusal of treatment by the patient's family
options.D: Intentional sabotage by a single disgruntled worker

explanation: Errors usually happen when several safety checks fail all at the same time, letting a mistake reach the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T8#GNS312_U5_T8_h4)

question: An older patient struggles to button their shirts because of stiff fingers from arthritis. What is the best nursing action to help them stay independent?

options.A: Insist that a family member dress the patient daily
options.B: Recommend adaptive clothing fasteners like Velcro
options.C: Tell the patient to stop wearing shirts altogether
options.D: Transfer the patient to a long-term care facility

explanation: Fantastic nursing thinking! Adaptive tools like Velcro help patients do things for themselves, boosting their confidence and maintaining their dignity. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h6)

question: How do many Nigerian families typically approach end-of-life decisions compared to Western models?

options.A: By leaving all choices entirely to junior hospital staff
options.B: Through a communal approach involving extended family members
options.C: By signing formal living wills upon hospital admission
options.D: By avoiding discussions about death and dying completely

explanation: In many Nigerian and African cultures, health decisions are rarely made alone. They are usually discussed and decided together as an extended family unit. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the main reason for putting an artificial airway in an unconscious patient?

options.A: To prevent the tongue from sliding back during feeding
options.B: To allow the administration of oral liquid medications
options.C: To protect against aspiration and maintain clear breathing
options.D: To measure core body temperature continuously

explanation: You're doing great! Unconscious patients can't protect their airway or swallow properly, so a tube keeps air flowing and stops saliva or vomit from entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h7)

question: At what cervical dilation does the active phase of normal labor officially start on a partograph?

options.A: 8 centimeters
options.B: 10 centimeters
options.C: 1 centimeter
options.D: 4 centimeters

explanation: 4 centimeters is your magic marker! That is where the active phase of labor officially begins on the partograph. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h6)

question: In public health and community nursing, what age range defines the "girl child"?

options.A: From puberty to twenty-one years
options.B: From birth to twelve years
options.C: From infancy to five years
options.D: From birth to eighteen years

explanation: You'll often hear this in community postings! The girl child covers females from the day they are born until they turn 18, right before legal adulthood. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T5#GNS225_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which circumcision tool uses a small plastic ring tied over the foreskin that eventually falls off on its own?

options.A: Plastibell
options.B: Gomco clamp
options.C: Scalpel blade
options.D: Mogen clamp

explanation: That's the Plastibell! It stays snug on the tissue, cutting off blood supply to the extra skin so it drops off cleanly after a few days as it heals. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the term for the natural home where a germ lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: A transmission route
options.B: A reservoir
options.C: A susceptible host
options.D: A portal of exit

explanation: A reservoir acts as the primary habitat where microorganisms thrive and multiply before infecting a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the absolute first thing you must do when an adverse event happens?

options.A: Ensuring immediate patient safety and stabilization
options.B: Calling a lawyer to discuss legal liability
options.C: Writing down every detail in the official logbook
options.D: Notifying the hospital director immediately

explanation: Patient care always comes first! Before any paperwork or reports, we must make sure our patient is safe and stable. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h2)

question: What is the main difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: If they come from plant or animal sources
options.B: How fast they dissolve in the bloodstream
options.C: The total amount the body requires daily
options.D: Whether they can provide energy to the body

explanation: You got it! Macro means large (needed in grams), while micro means small (needed in tiny milligram or microgram amounts). [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using patient assistive devices in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the cost of long-term care stays
options.B: To help patients maintain independence and safety
options.C: To reduce hospital administration paperwork
options.D: To completely replace the need for nursing staff

explanation: You got this! Assistive devices are designed to empower patients, helping them move and care for themselves safely and with dignity. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h1)

question: Using the Plate Method for diabetes management, what should fill half of the dinner plate?

options.A: Full-fat dairy products
options.B: Starchy grains and yams
options.C: Lean protein foods
options.D: Non-starchy vegetables

explanation: Half of the plate should contain non-starchy vegetables to provide volume and fiber without raising blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe data security practice for a clinical nurse?

options.A: Leaving an active patient chart open on the screen while walking away
options.B: Keeping personal computer login passwords private and confidential
options.C: Logging out of the electronic health record station before taking a break
options.D: Reporting unfamiliar software pop-ups to the hospital IT department

explanation: Never leave an unattended terminal logged in! It allows unauthorized eyes to see or change confidential patient information. Always lock your screen. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)

question: In the classic formula (Desired over Have), what does the letter 'D' stand for?

options.A: Daily maximum limit
options.B: Drop factor of the IV set
options.C: Dilution volume
options.D: Desired dose ordered by the prescriber

explanation: 'D' is simply what the doctor Desires (ordered) for the patient to receive. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h6)

question: A clinic makes sure patients from all backgrounds receive the exact same high standard of treatment. Which quality dimension is this?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Efficiency
options.C: Timeliness
options.D: Effectiveness

explanation: Well done! Equity means fairness—ensuring every patient gets great, high-quality care regardless of their background, status, or wealth. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is ongoing tracking, while evaluation assesses final results
options.B: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses on buildings
options.C: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.D: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is completely free

explanation: You've got it! Monitoring happens step-by-step as the project runs, while evaluation looks at the big picture after it's done. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h7)

question: Which two body systems share the use of the male urethra?

options.A: Digestive and urinary
options.B: Urinary and reproductive
options.C: Lymphatic and circulatory
options.D: Respiratory and endocrine

explanation: The male urethra pulls double duty! It acts as a passageway for passing urine from the bladder and for expelling semen. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why might a single medication belong to more than one distinct category?

options.A: Because it can be classified by its chemical structure or disease treated
options.B: Because doctors use random methods to sort medications
options.C: Because drug companies change the name of the drug every year
options.D: Because government laws require multiple names for safety

explanation: A drug can be sorted differently based on how it is made, how it acts in the body, or the specific illness it targets. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h1)

question: A patient at 32 weeks reports she has not felt her baby move all day. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Mild physiological anemia of pregnancy
options.B: Potential fetal distress or compromise
options.C: Standard weight gain in the third trimester
options.D: Normal resting behavior of a mature fetus

explanation: Whenever a mom says baby's movements have stopped or slowed right down, treat it as an emergency and check the baby right away. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h7)

question: What is a critical rule to follow regarding promises made to disaster survivors?

options.A: Promise that all their family members are safe
options.B: Tell them the government will pay for everything
options.C: Never make promises you cannot guarantee to keep
options.D: Promise them a new home to make them feel better

explanation: False promises destroy trust and increase anxiety when reality turns out differently. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of ergonomics in the workplace?

options.A: Inspecting the concrete strength of the building
options.B: Setting exact employee salaries and bonuses
options.C: Fitting workstations and tools to match human body limits
options.D: Managing the menu in the staff cafeteria

explanation: Exactly! Ergonomics is all about designing work tools and chairs to fit the human body, preventing physical strain. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h7)

question: After cleaning the skin with an antiseptic and before giving the numbing injection, what is the next important step?

options.A: Suturing the edges of the anticipated wound
options.B: Placing sterile surgical drapes over the patient
options.C: Applying direct pressure to collapse blood vessels
options.D: Allowing the antiseptic solution to dry completely

explanation: Patience is key! Antiseptics need a little air-drying time to actually kill the germs before the skin barrier is opened up. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T3#GNS213_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why do nurse managers love doing regular audits of clinic referral records?

options.A: They help identify service gaps, referral trends, and lost patients
options.B: They prove that the clinic requires no further government funding
options.C: They automatically generate transport money for emergency cases
options.D: They ensure that nurses never make mistakes on patient folders

explanation: You've got this! Regular checks show us patterns in patient transfers and highlight where our community care or tracking needs a little boost. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h8)

question: What is a major communication benefit of implementing MBO in a clinical setting?

options.A: It allows doctors to bypass nurses when giving patient orders
options.B: It completely replaces all written patient health records
options.C: It opens up constructive feedback channels between staff and management
options.D: It stops patients from complaining about hospital food

explanation: Structured check-ins give nurses a reliable voice to discuss operational roadblocks with directors. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when collecting data?

options.A: Training all data collectors thoroughly before starting
options.B: Securing formal institutional approvals from management
options.C: Pilot testing questionnaires on a small sample group
options.D: Discarding digital backups immediately to save storage space

question: Why is every single link in the chain of infection important for a disease to spread?

options.A: Germs require all links simultaneously to grow larger
options.B: The host becomes immune if a link is missing
options.C: Pathogens cannot survive outside the reservoir link
options.D: Breaking any single link stops the cycle of infection

explanation: Think of it like a chain: if you break just one link, the infection cannot travel further. That is why simple actions like handwashing are so powerful! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why are ointment-based topical medications usually preferred over creams for thick, scaly skin lesions?

options.A: Ointments can be applied in very thick layers without any side effects
options.B: Ointments trap moisture effectively and penetrate thick skin better
options.C: Ointments dry out quickly and prevent any staining of clothing
options.D: Ointments wash off easily with plain water during normal bathing

explanation: The heavy, oil-based nature of ointments creates a barrier that locks in moisture, making them ideal for dry, thickened, or hyperkeratotic skin conditions. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h3)

question: When is the best time to record a patient's vital signs in their chart?

options.A: At the very end of the working shift
options.B: Whenever the physician asks for past notes
options.C: Only if the patient shows abnormal symptoms
options.D: Promptly after completing the assessment

explanation: Always document right away! Doing it immediately prevents mix-ups and keeps patient care safe and reliable. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h9)

question: How do out-of-pocket payment systems negatively affect maternal health?

options.A: They cause families to delay seeking emergency medical treatment
options.B: They motivate nurses to work longer shifts without resting
options.C: They ensure that wealthy patients subsidize free community care
options.D: They improve the distribution of drugs in primary clinics

question: What is the main goal of doing a dietary assessment in a community?

options.A: To understand the regular food intake and eating patterns of families
options.B: To calculate the exact financial income of every household
options.C: To determine the water sanitation index of the village
options.D: To diagnose infectious diseases like malaria and typhoid

explanation: Great! By asking about what families normally eat, nurses can spot missing nutrients and help plan practical solutions. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which group is especially at risk during emergencies because disasters easily disrupt their medications and daily routines?

options.A: Emergency medical technicians
options.B: Professional disaster relief volunteers
options.C: Young healthy adults with stable employment
options.D: Individuals with pre-existing mental illness

explanation: Well done! People managing mental health conditions are very vulnerable during crises because losing access to their medications and support systems can trigger a relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of the fallopian tubes in the female body?

options.C: To secrete large amounts of protective progesterone
options.D: To produce the monthly supply of mature oocytes

question: What is the main focus of Psychological First Aid (PFA) in a disaster?

options.A: Providing humane practical support and reducing distress
options.B: Conducting formal psychoanalysis sessions
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications
options.D: Diagnosing deep psychiatric disorders

explanation: Well done! PFA isn't about heavy therapy or psychoanalysis; it's about being human, offering practical comfort, and helping people feel safe. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h7)

question: A patient with a history of asthma is admitted for post-abortion care. What is your most important first step?

options.A: Discharging the patient with an inhaler
options.B: Starting intravenous antibiotic therapy
options.C: Establishing accurate baseline vital signs
options.D: Restricting all oral fluids immediately

explanation: Getting accurate baseline vitals gives you a starting point so you can quickly spot any sudden changes in breathing or circulation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h2)

question: What tragic emotional outcome is sometimes seen among young brides who feel completely trapped with no way out?

options.A: Bipolar manic episodes
options.B: Suicide and self-harm
options.C: Dissociative identity disorder
options.D: Pathological compulsive gambling

explanation: That's correct. Overwhelming hopelessness and a lack of support drive some desperate young brides to self-harm or suicide. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T11#GNS312_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which simple tip helps your body absorb oral albendazole much better?

options.C: Avoiding all fluids for two hours after dosing
options.D: Taking the pill on an empty stomach with vinegar

question: What do the letters in the FAST stroke mnemonic stand for to help recognize warning signs?

options.A: Fluid intake, Activity level, Skin turgor, Eyes check
options.B: Fast breathing, Airway blockage, Sound tone, Temperature
options.C: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call
options.D: Fever, Aches, Stiffness, Tiredness

explanation: FAST is a simple public health tool used to spot the most common stroke symptoms quickly. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h6)

question: What do we mean by 'closed-loop communication' during a busy medical emergency?

options.A: Repeating a delegated instruction back to the sender to confirm it was heard and understood
options.B: Writing all verbal orders on a whiteboard before speaking to team members
options.C: Turning off all ward intercoms so outside noise does not distract the team
options.D: Locking the patient room door so unauthorized staff cannot enter

explanation: Exactly! Saying 'Got it, giving 10mg IV now' back to the doctor or senior nurse prevents dangerous mistakes in high-stress moments. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h6)

question: What famous global health goal was established at the 1978 Alma-Ata conference?

options.A: Eradication of Malaria by 1985
options.B: Universal Hospital Access by 1990
options.C: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.D: Free Tertiary Care for Every Citizen

explanation: The Alma-Ata conference set the ambitious global target of achieving 'Health for All by the Year 2000' through primary health care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which official council regulates the practice and licensing of midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Community Board
options.B: National Union of Local Government Employees
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Medical and Dental Association of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the body that sets our professional standards, trains us, and gives us our licenses to practice safely. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T3#GNS225_U3_T3_h8)

question: Which two vaccines are routinely given to newborns right at birth in Nigeria?

options.A: BCG and Oral Polio Vaccine zero
options.B: Pentavalent and Tetanus toxoid
options.C: Hepatitis A and Rabies vaccine
options.D: Measles and Yellow Fever vaccine

explanation: Exactly! Right after delivery, babies receive the BCG shot against tuberculosis and their first drops of oral polio vaccine (OPV 0). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h2)

question: What is the primary function of an antibody in the human body?

options.A: To produce energy for cellular reactions
options.B: To carry oxygen to body tissues
options.C: To identify and neutralize foreign antigens
options.D: To clot blood after an injury occurs

explanation: Antibodies are immune proteins designed to bind specifically to foreign invaders and toxins, marking them for destruction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h1)

question: What happens to a pregnant woman's total body water and blood volume?

options.A: They increase by up to fifty percent
options.B: They fluctuate wildly on a daily basis
options.C: They decrease significantly due to fluid loss
options.D: They remain completely unchanged throughout gestation

explanation: Pregnancy causes the body to hold onto a lot more fluid! Blood volume can jump by nearly half, which helps dilute and spread out medications. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which organ handles oxygen and waste exchange for the baby before birth?

options.A: The placenta
options.B: The fetal kidneys
options.C: The fetal liver
options.D: The amniotic sac

explanation: Before birth, the placenta acts as the baby's lungs and kidneys, bringing in oxygen and clearing waste through the umbilical cord. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h1)

question: A patient gets a drug that blocks opioid receptors and stops other narcotics from binding, but it only causes mild pain relief. What is this called?

options.A: Enzyme inhibitor
options.B: Pure antagonist
options.C: Full agonist
options.D: Partial agonist

question: Which core principle of health advocacy is all about fair distribution of health resources?

options.A: Patient autonomy
options.B: Clinical competence
options.C: Strict confidentiality
options.D: Social justice

explanation: Spot on! Social justice is about making sure health resources actually reach the people who need them most, keeping things fair and equal. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of subjective data collection during a musculoskeletal assessment?

options.A: Checking laboratory test results for inflammation
options.B: Measuring exact joint angles with a goniometer
options.C: The patient's personal experience of symptoms
options.D: Testing deep tendon reflexes in the limbs

explanation: Subjective data relies on what the patient tells you about their pain, stiffness, and how symptoms affect their daily life. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h1)

question: What makes a person's blood type classified as Rh-positive?

options.A: The lack of any proteins on the cell surface
options.B: The presence of anti-Rh antibodies in the plasma
options.C: The presence of the D antigen on red blood cells
options.D: The ability to donate blood to anyone safely

explanation: The main determinant of Rh-positive status is finding the D antigen on the surface of the red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is the moving ambulance considered a difficult environment for clinical assessments?

options.A: Patients are always unconscious and unable to speak during transit
options.B: Medical equipment completely stops working inside motorized vehicles
options.C: Vibration, road noise, and cramped space interfere with standard checks
options.D: Natural lighting makes it impossible to see skin color changes

explanation: Motion, noise, and physical constraints make hearing breath sounds or palpating faint pulses much harder than in a quiet hospital bed. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h1)

question: What do we mean by the 'halo effect' when grading students?

options.A: Using computer software to grade practical nursing procedures
options.B: Failing to evaluate a student due to a lack of time on the ward
options.C: Giving every student a failing grade because of one minor mistake
options.D: Allowing one positive trait of a student to unfairly influence the entire evaluation

explanation: The halo effect happens when a student's polite smile or charm makes an instructor overlook their clinical mistakes. We want objective grading! [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h6)

question: What symptom makes vitamin B12 deficiency different from simple iron deficiency?

options.A: Elevation in total white blood cell counts
options.B: Severe swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Presence of neurological symptoms like numbness
options.D: Rapid drop in liver enzyme production

question: A patient with severe anxiety keeps relapsing shortly after returning home from the hospital. What should you look at next?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop worrying about family issues
options.B: Discontinuing all medications immediately
options.C: Evaluating ongoing stressors and triggers in the home environment
options.D: Focusing solely on hospital food preferences

question: What can happen if you use a sensitive smart bed alarm on a patient who is fully independent and active?

options.B: Unnecessary anxiety for the patient and alarm fatigue for nurses
options.C: Automatic cancellation of physician medication orders
options.D: Rapid depletion of the bed's internal backup battery

explanation: If a bed keeps beeping every time an active patient moves, it stresses the patient out and trains staff to ignore the noise—which is called alarm fatigue! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h3)

question: What equipment do you need to measure the height (length) of a child who is under two years old?

options.A: Flexible cloth tape
options.B: Hanging spring scale
options.C: Infant length board
options.D: Vertical stadiometer

question: What is the main job of myosin light chain kinase (MLCK)?

options.A: To pump calcium back into storage sites

options.C: To connect adjacent muscle fibers together
options.D: To phosphorylate myosin heads so they can bind to actin

question: Why do fat-soluble hormones need carrier proteins to travel in the blood?

options.A: Carrier proteins are needed to digest the hormone
options.B: They do not mix well with the watery plasma
options.C: They are too heavy to float without assistance
options.D: They would instantly destroy red blood cells if free

explanation: Oil and water don't mix! Since fat-soluble hormones don't dissolve in watery blood plasma, they need special carrier proteins to give them a ride through the circulatory system. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h6)

question: How can a nurse best help a hospitalized older adult with severe arthritis eat on their own?

options.A: Insist that family members visit during every single mealtime
options.B: Feed the patient all meals to ensure they finish every single bite
options.C: Serve only pureed foods that require no physical chewing effort
options.D: Provide adaptive eating utensils like weighted handles or plate guards

explanation: Brilliant! Adaptive tools help work around stiff joints and tremors, letting patients keep their independence and dignity at mealtime. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T014#GNS227_U2_T014_h6)

question: How should a nurse collect a urine sample from a patient with a catheter?

options.A: By disconnecting the catheter tubing from the drainage bag
options.B: From the rubber sampling port using a sterile syringe
options.C: By squeezing urine backward from the tubing into the bladder
options.D: From the bottom valve of the plastic collection bag

explanation: Always use the special needleless sampling port with a sterile syringe. Never take urine from the drainage bag, as those germs have been sitting there and won't give an accurate lab result! [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why does the surface of the brain have so many folds and grooves?

options.A: To improve the circulation of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: To increase the surface area for more neurons
options.C: To separate the left and right sides of the body
options.D: To absorb physical shock from head injuries

explanation: Folding packs a massive amount of brain power into a small space, giving us room for lots of nerve cells! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h2)

question: How does knowledge happen when using intuition?

options.A: By reading old medical journals in the hospital library
options.B: Through strict adherence to hospital procedure manuals
options.C: By performing a double-blind randomized clinical trial
options.D: Through an immediate gut feeling or hunch without conscious reasoning

explanation: Intuition skips the slow steps of logic and gives you a sudden inner sense that something is right (or wrong). [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h4)

question: A nurse is cleaning a gastrointestinal endoscope after a patient procedure. How should this tool be processed using the Spaulding system?

options.A: Dry heat sterilization in an oven
options.B: Simple rinse under cold tap water
options.C: High-level chemical disinfection
options.D: Low-level surface wipe with alcohol

explanation: Because endoscopes touch mucous membranes, they fall into the semi-critical category and need high-level disinfection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why do children need especially fast nursing action during emergencies compared to adults?

options.A: Children are always more cooperative with nursing staff than adults
options.B: Children never experience true medical emergencies
options.C: Pediatric equipment is much harder to find in a standard hospital
options.D: Children have smaller physical reserves and deteriorate much faster

explanation: Because children have lower physical reserves, a minor illness or breathing problem can quickly turn serious if we don't catch it early. You're building great clinical intuition! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h4)

question: What exactly is a vesicovaginal fistula (VVF)?

options.A: An abnormal opening between the bladder and the vagina
options.B: A blockage in the tube carrying urine from the kidney
options.C: A complete failure of the kidneys to produce urine
options.D: An infection of the lining inside the urinary bladder

explanation: You nailed it! A VVF creates an unwanted channel between these two organs, which is why urine leaks through continuously. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: Why is it smart for a nurse to watch a patient do tasks when they are tired?

options.A: It proves the patient is malingering and refusing to participate
options.B: Fatigue helps nurses determine the exact surgical date for discharge
options.C: Real-world environments often test patients when their energy is depleted
options.D: Hospital regulations require endurance testing prior to every meal

explanation: Makes total sense! Anyone can look great in the morning, but safety issues pop up when fatigue sets in later in the day. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h3)
